newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest hydropower cutbacks seen easing Fri.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest hydropower cutbacks seen easing Fri.

text.p: Flow cutbacks at hydroelectric dams in the U.S. Northwest are expected to ease by Friday as recent heavy rainfall abates, sources at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Portland, Ore., said Thursday.
Flows at the Grand Coulee dam on the Columbia River have been trimmed to help out the lower sections of the river and the smaller Willamette River from overflowing.

But the cuts were described as slight, with Grand Coulee running near 93,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) Wednesday and Thursday, compared with 115,000 cfs on Monday and 103,000 cfs on Tuesday, the Corps of Engineers said.
"We typically cut flows at the weekend anyway," the source noted.

She added that reservoirs in general remain at or above flood control levels, and dam flows will be increased over the next couple of weeks - barring further rainstorms - in order to bring them down to target volumes.
